config.title: Test Context

intro.title: Test Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that uses the Context API to share data between components without passing props manually. You will learn how to create a context, provide its value from a parent component, and consume it in child components. The main technologies involved are React's createContext, Provider, and useContext hook. This will help you understand how to manage global state efficiently in a React app.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, testing React components with Context is essential for building maintainable user interfaces that rely on shared state. For example, in e-commerce platforms, product filtering components need to access the same filter state across multiple UI sections like sidebars, product grids, and breadcrumbs. Similarly, dashboard applications use Context to manage user authentication state, allowing components like navigation menus, profile panels, and permission-based modals to consistently reflect login status. By testing these Context-dependent components, developers ensure that state changes propagate correctly, preventing bugs in complex, interactive features like multi-step forms or real-time data visualizations.

objectives: Initialize a React context with default values
Construct a context provider component to wrap application sections
Implement a custom hook to consume context values in child components
Configure multiple components to share state through context
Update context values from nested child components
Manipulate context data to reflect user interactions
Render components that dynamically respond to context changes

steps.title: Import React and createContext
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and createContext from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';

seedCode.App.jsx: // Import React and createContext from 'react' here

steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports to use React and the createContext API.
successCriteria: React and createContext are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and createContext from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and createContext from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create a context with a default value
steps.instruction: Create a context using createContext() with a default value of 'Guest' and export it as TestContext.
steps.hint: Call createContext with a string default value and assign it to a const variable. Then export it.

seedCode.App.jsx:
import React, { createContext } from 'react';

// Create a context with default value 'Guest' and export it as TestContext

steps.expectedOutcome: A context object named TestContext is created with a default value and exported.
successCriteria: TestContext is defined using createContext('Guest') and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using createContext with 'Guest' as the default value and exporting it as TestContext.
steps.feedbackWrong: The context wasn't created correctly. Use createContext('Guest') and export the result.

steps.title: Create a provider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TestProvider that accepts children as props and returns them wrapped in TestContext.Provider.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes children as a prop and returns <TestContext.Provider value={someValue}>{children}</TestContext.Provider>. For now, use the default value 'Guest' for the value prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TestProvider component is defined that wraps children in TestContext.Provider with the value 'Guest'.
successCriteria: TestProvider component is created, accepts children prop, and returns TestContext.Provider with value='Guest' wrapping children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component accepts children as a prop and returns TestContext.Provider with value='Guest' wrapping {children}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a component named TestProvider that takes children and returns <TestContext.Provider value='Guest'>{children}</TestContext.Provider>.

steps.title: Add state to the provider
steps.instruction: Import useState from 'react' and add a state variable to your provider component to manage the context value.
steps.hint: Add the useState import alongside createContext, then declare a state variable inside your provider component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The provider component will have a state variable that can hold the dynamic context value.
successCriteria: useState is imported from 'react' and a state variable is declared inside the provider component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported useState and declared a state variable inside the provider component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported useState from 'react' and added a state variable declaration to your provider component.

steps.title: Pass state value through context
steps.instruction: Inside the provider component, wrap the children prop with the TestContext.Provider component and pass the state value as the value prop.
steps.hint: Use the TestContext.Provider component to wrap the children and provide the current state value to all child components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The provider component now wraps its children with TestContext.Provider and passes the user state as the value prop, making the state available to all child components.
successCriteria: TestContext.Provider wraps the children prop and receives the user state as its value prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to wrap the children prop with TestContext.Provider and pass the user state as the value prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provider component should wrap its children with TestContext.Provider and pass the user state as the value prop. Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Create a consumer component
steps.instruction: Create a separate functional component named TestConsumer that will consume the context values. Make it return a div element for now.
steps.hint: Define a new component that will later use the TestContext. Start with a simple structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a new TestConsumer component ready to consume context values in later steps.
successCriteria: A TestConsumer component is created with a function declaration or arrow function, and it returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a component named TestConsumer that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a separate component named TestConsumer with a return statement containing a div element.

steps.title: Import useContext in consumer
steps.instruction: Import the useContext hook from 'react' in your consumer component file.
steps.hint: You need to add useContext to the existing import statement from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a hook
import React, { useState, useContext } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The useContext hook is imported alongside createContext in the import statement.
successCriteria: useContext is imported from 'react' in the import statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure useContext is included in the import statement from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useContext hook needs to be imported from 'react' to access context values.

steps.title: Access context value with useContext
steps.instruction: Inside the consumer component, call useContext with TestContext to get the current user value and store it in a variable.
steps.hint: Use the useContext hook with the TestContext object you imported earlier.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessing context value
const currentValue = useContext(MyContext);
steps.expectedOutcome: The consumer component now has access to the current context value through the useContext hook.
successCriteria: The consumer component calls useContext with TestContext and stores the result in a variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useContext with TestContext as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try using the useContext hook with TestContext to get the current user value.

steps.title: Display context value in JSX
steps.instruction: Inside the TestConsumer component, return JSX that displays the user value you accessed with useContext.
steps.hint:
Use curly braces {} to embed the user value in your JSX, like

{user}

.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TestConsumer component now returns JSX that renders the current context value.
successCriteria: TestConsumer returns JSX containing the user value from context.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning JSX that includes the user value from context.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TestConsumer component should return JSX that displays the user value from context.

steps.title: Wrap app with provider
steps.instruction: In the TestProvider component, wrap the children prop with TestContext.Provider and pass the user state as the value prop.
steps.hint: Use the TestContext.Provider component as a wrapper around children, and set its value prop to user.
steps.expectedOutcome: The provider component now makes the user state available to any child component via context.
successCriteria: TestProvider returns TestContext.Provider with children inside and value={user}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning TestContext.Provider with the children prop inside and setting value to user.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provider component needs to return TestContext.Provider wrapping children with value={user}.
